research_question: Can a task-ID-free relational state signature and state-dependent sparse residual beat v6; if not, does an uncertainty-aware ensemble provide a scientifically better world model without another latent router?

literature_mapping.paper: QORA: Zero-Shot Transfer via Interpretable Object-Relational Model Learning, ICML 2024
literature_mapping.repo_hypothesis: Replace lexical/domain routing with a compact relation-state signature that can transfer across held-out tasks.

literature_mapping.paper: DSMoE: Matrix-Partitioned Experts with Dynamic Routing, EMNLP 2025
literature_mapping.repo_hypothesis: Route each visible state to exactly two basis residuals instead of assigning one expert to an entire domain.

literature_mapping.paper: Is a Modular Architecture Enough?, NeurIPS 2022
literature_mapping.repo_hypothesis: Require utilization and entropy diagnostics and compare against an equal-input, parameter-matched dense control.

literature_mapping.paper: PETS: Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Handful of Trials using Probabilistic Dynamics Models, NeurIPS 2018
literature_mapping.repo_hypothesis: If routing fails, change direction to a uniform deep ensemble that exposes epistemic disagreement and improves predictive distributions.

stage_e1.hypothesis: A non-lexical relation-state signature with top-2 dynamic basis residuals removes the coarse-domain interference seen in v9 and beats both v6 and a parameter-matched dense signature model.

stage_e2_direction_switch.hypothesis: The limiting factor is irreducible and epistemic uncertainty rather than missing latent capacity; a uniform probabilistic ensemble improves task-disjoint predictive distributions and identifies model errors.
stage_e2_direction_switch.mechanism: Three independent v6 teacher-plus-residual members per ensemble; uniform probability mixture; predictive entropy and member mutual information reported separately; no confirmation-tuned weights or thresholds.
